originalAlarm.description: The value written to `&x` is never used.

reasoning: FALSE POSITIVE: The alarm reports 'int x = *length' (line 31) as a dead store — x is assigned but never used — when CONFIG_SECURITY=false. In the real Linux reiserfs_security_init() code, x (the dereferenced length value) is used for security attribute size processing. The simplified file stripped those uses. This is a simplification artifact. The known vbdb bug for 30e053248da.c is UninitializedVariable when !SECURITY: security_old_inode_init_security() for !SECURITY always returns 0 without writing *len, so 'length' in reiserfs_create() remains uninitialized; 'int x = *length' at line 31 then reads an uninitialized value. The tool did not detect the uninitialized read and instead reported only the dead store on x.
